solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Piece of food — prize for winning cat?

parts.note: a medal is the award handed to a victor
a lion is the big cat of the savannah

explanation.surface: A gourmet wonders whether a tasty morsel would make a fitting trophy for a champion cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey reading: a champion lion would earn a medal, giving MEDAL LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a small round cut of meat, such as a medallion of beef or pork.

clue.text: Dog tracks bones, to polish off

indicators.note: to track is to follow, so the dog's letters come after the doctor's

parts.note: sawbones is slang for a doctor, and MO is the Medical Officer
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A dog follows a scent to some bones and finishes them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like the dog's snack but is short for sawbones, a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off or deal with the remaining part of something.

clue.text: Clubs, in the end, start to latch on to sports event

indicators.note: the clubs letter is set inside the word for the end

parts.note: death is the end of life
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone in a sports event finally grabs a set of golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally', but 'in' is the container signal and 'the end' is DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest of ten events held over two days.

clue.text: Legendary lawman one phoned in middle of alert

indicators.note: the words for one and phoned go inside the central letters of alert
the letters of alert minus its first and last are used

parts.note: taken as written
to ring someone is to phone them, past tense rang

explanation.surface: A famous sheriff gets a phone call in the middle of an emergency alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alert' is not a call to be watchful here: only its middle letters are used, split around the phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Ranger is the masked hero of the American Western radio and TV series.

clue.text: Capless ball-point pen kept in pub's chained

indicators.note: the trimmed pen is held inside the word for the pub's

parts.note: an inn is a pub, so pub's gives INNS

indicators.note: the pen loses its top letter, as a pen without its cap

parts.note: Biro is the British brand name for a ball-point pen

explanation.surface: A ball-point pen lacking its cap is left behind at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is a British brand name that has become the everyday word for any ball-point pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner in irons is shackled with fetters, so the phrase means chained up.

clue.text: Clean-living type taking responsibility, short anorak outside

indicators.note: the shortened anorak goes around the word for responsibility
the final letter is dropped from the word for anorak

parts.note: anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a nerd
an onus is a burden or duty

explanation.surface: A virtuous person takes on a duty while wearing a cut-down rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anorak' looks like a coat, but in British slang it is a geek.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-user is someone who abstains from drugs, hence a clean-living person.

clue.text: Matches studied to grasp this?

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within their letters, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Games that are closely analysed in order to master them: what sort of game is this?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the game, whose matches are studied in depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess players famously study past games to understand the strategy of the board game.

clue.text: Fellow flanker for Harlequins in headgear

indicators.note: the edge letter is placed inside the word for headgear

parts.note: a cap is a hat

indicators.note: a flanker stands at the side, here the opening letter of the rugby club name

explanation.surface: A rugby flanker for the Harlequins club pulls on a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club and a flanker is a forward position; here 'flanker' means its edge letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal word for a man or fellow.

clue.text: County executives peripherally join congress

indicators.note: only the letters at the edges of the word are taken

parts.note: congress can mean sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: Company bosses in a county agree to merge with a legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks political but is used in its old sense of sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is a county in the east of England, north-east of London.

clue.text: European finally strode out for fag

parts.note: a Slav is a member of an eastern European people

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is used

parts.note: away means not at home, out

explanation.surface: A European strides out to buy a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British for a cigarette but also for tiring work, which is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English fag means a tiring chore, so to fag is to toil hard.

clue.text: Drink needed, following exercise nut

indicators.note: the drink comes after the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
a can is a container of drink such as beer

explanation.surface: After a workout, a thirsty athlete needs a drink, then a snack of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is the edible nut of a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: FT setter turned sienna shade (mid-section only) here in the Med

parts.note: Io is another setter of the Financial Times crossword

indicators.note: the letters of the colour word are turned around into a new order
just the central letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A crossword setter paints a Mediterranean scene in burnt-sienna tones.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is a fellow FT compiler. SIENNA is rearranged to NIANSE, and the middle letter of SHADE gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian Sea is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and southern Italy.

clue.text: Cambridge college preferred her mixing with English stream

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, the preferred one

indicators.note: the three letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A woman likes to mingle by an English river near Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Ouse runs through York; several English rivers share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Peterhouse is the oldest college of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1284.

clue.text: Chopper draws in left wheel section

indicators.note: the cutting tool takes the abbreviation inside itself

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool

explanation.surface: A helicopter pulls in on the left, its wheel visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but it is the tool, AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which a wheel turns, part of the wheel assembly.

clue.text: Idiot from navy putting most of wages on deck

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: income is money earned, wages
the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A naval fool gambles most of his pay on a card game on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a pack of cards, but it is the poop deck of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a foolish or stupid person.

clue.text: Greek deity is rebuffed, man briefly states audibly

annotationWithheld.clue: Greek deity is rebuffed, man briefly states audibly

clue.text: American upset hairstyle in one type of car

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US
a perm is a permanent wave, a hairstyle
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American is annoyed by the hairstyle she got in one kind of car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like distress but turns US upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermini is a small hatchback class of car, such as the Ford Fiesta.

clue.text: Stylish pair of boots available in green? It's an impossible target

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the word for green

parts.note: raw means inexperienced, green
in means fashionable

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Fashionable boots on sale in green, but are they an unachievable goal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing rainbows' means pursuing something unattainable, which is why the definition fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of the rainbow can never be reached, so it stands for an unattainable goal.

clue.text: Portion of ice-cream runs through kitchenware and walls?

parts.note: a brick is a block of ice cream

indicators.note: the letter for runs passes through the pan

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A block of ice cream drips through the pans and down the kitchen walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks walls as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brickwork is masonry made of bricks, the stuff walls are typically built from.

clue.text: One with two poles entered training with Olympian target, ultimately

definitions.text: One with two poles entered training with Olympian target, ultimately

indicators.note: the pieces for one and the poles go inside the training letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
I is the Roman numeral for one
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A rower with two oars began training with the Olympics as his goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Pinsent is a British rower with four Olympic golds; the whole clue describes him. 'Two poles' means the compass points north and south, not oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinsent trained as an oarsman aiming for Olympic gold, which he won four times.

clue.text: Nathaniel, covered in fat, rejected health problem

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole is reversed
the short name is enclosed by the word for fat

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
Nat is a short form of Nathaniel

explanation.surface: A man smothered in fat suffers a serious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered in' encloses the name, and 'rejected' turns the whole result back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, a serious medical condition.

clue.text: Devious guards regularly eat cake in an eccentric manner

indicators.note: the word for devious holds the picked letters within it

parts.note: wily means cunning, devious

indicators.note: every other letter of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Sneaky sentries keep eating cake in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like sentries but is the container signal; 'regularly' picks letters across both words as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacky means zany or odd, so its adverb describes behaving in a strange way.

clue.text: I'm unhappy with old English semi that's converted

indicators.note: the letters of the house word are converted into another order

explanation.surface: A gloomy owner of an old English semi-detached house that's been converted.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI is rearranged to ISME. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is me is an old exclamation of sorrow or self-pity.

clue.text: Kids' food? Back of hamper next to river

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper sits at the back by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags kids as baby children: a rusk is a hard biscuit for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a dry biscuit given to babies who are teething.

clue.text: Prince of Wales, making Sabbath priority? Hogwash

indicators.note: the Sabbath letter is given priority, going in front

parts.note: William, Prince of Wales, is Will for short

explanation.surface: The heir to the throne decides to put Sunday observance first: nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: Hogwash is both nonsense and pig food, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is kitchen waste fed to pigs, the literal sense of hogwash.

clue.text: Labourer having beef about wood centre in Somerset

indicators.note: the meat word goes around the tree word

parts.note: steak is a cut of beef
elm is a type of wood

indicators.note: the two central letters of the county name are taken

explanation.surface: A worker in Somerset has a grievance about timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' suggests a grievance, but it is meat. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelmaker is a worker in a steel mill, a manual labourer.

clue.text: Staff accepted French manual worker

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
in means accepted, as in being in with a group

explanation.surface: A French workman takes up a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor; working with his hands made him a manual worker, in a playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin was a French sculptor who shaped clay and stone with his hands.

clue.text: European runner recalled run, wearing medal

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole is read in reverse
the honour has the letter for run on it, as if worn

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A European athlete is called back after running while wearing a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a river, not an athlete. R inside OBE gives ORBE, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a river in north-east Spain, and rivers run.

clue.text: Novelist has vacuous idea in margins

indicators.note: empty of content, so the inner letters are removed

parts.note: banks are the margins or edges of a river

explanation.surface: A writer has an empty notion scribbled in the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Banks was a Scottish novelist who wrote The Wasp Factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Iain Banks was a Scottish author of literary and science fiction novels.

clue.text: Eggy bit of omelette consumed by poet

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed by the poet's name

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A poet eats a scrap of an omelette.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, from the Latin ovum for egg.

clue.text: One discussed cement for house

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: talked about, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: glue is an adhesive, a cement

explanation.surface: A builder talks about cement for a new house.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome-shaped house built from snow blocks.

clue.text: Lady records earliest of kestrels, wearing coat

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: A woman plays records about kestrels while wearing a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat or jacket made from sheep's pelt.
